what_it_is.value: A hybrid option, not a released product: TD keeps alacritty_terminal 0.26 (the Alacritty project's Rust crate) as the only text grid and feeds the same PTY bytes to a second emulator, libghostty-vt (Ghostty's Zig VT core, maintained by the Ghostty project and reached through Uzaaft's `libghostty-vt` Rust bindings), used only for its Kitty image store and placement list; TD's renderer paints those placements over alacritty's cells.
what_it_is.note: quote: "API for inspecting images and placements stored via the [Kitty graphics protocol](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/graphics-protocol/). The central object is @ref GhosttyKittyGraphics, an opaque handle to the image storage associated with a terminal's active screen. From it you can iterate over placements and look up individual images." — [measured] libghostty-vt's C header at the commit the crates.io bindings pin; this is the API the shadow would read. That no product runs this hybrid is under adoption. The option itself is TD's own construction, not a project.

At the crates.io 0.2.1 pin (ghostty a887df4) libghostty-vt covers: transmission t=d/f/t/s, where f, t and s are off by default in the library build and TD must enable each one; formats f=24/32/100, where PNG works only with a TD-supplied decoder callback; zlib compression (o=z); direct placements (a=T/a=p) held on tracked pins and virtual U=1 placements; deletes a/i/n/c/f/p/q/r/x/y/z; a=q query replies; and z-index layers exposed as BELOW_BG/BELOW_TEXT/ABOVE_TEXT. Quota: 10 MB by default in the library build, set by the embedder.

Placement geometry moves with scrolling, so TD must recompute positions on every dirty frame.

If unchanged, the placement set and all image data are identical and both placement snapshots and per-image staleness checks can be skipped. state_snapshot.value: No, not for pictures. TD's gridwire::encode_snapshot re-encodes only alacritty's grid as VT bytes. libghostty-vt's own binary snapshot (C API added upstream on 2026-08-03, after crate 0.2.1's pin) says Kitty image and placement state is not part of it. So a re-attaching window would get text and no pictures unless TD ships image bytes and placements itself. The window's replica also cannot re-parse t=t or t=s transmissions, because the protocol makes the first terminal that reads them, the host's shadow, delete the file or unlink the shared memory.
state_snapshot.note: quote: "// Kitty image and placement state is not part of this snapshot // version, but the placeholder is still a valid Unicode scalar." — [measured] libghostty's snapshot encoder on main. The deletion rule is in the kitty protocol doc (https://github.com/kovidgoyal/kitty/blob/42d3cb2148acc182946901091dbbb0431a5a3344/docs/graphics-protocol.rst#L332-L344): "A temporary file, the terminal emulator will delete the file after reading the pixel data" and, for shared memory, "The terminal emulator must read the data from the memory object and then unlink and close it on POSIX". gridwire.rs (TD) documents a text-only snapshot.

threading_and_loop.value: The loop is split. alacritty's EventLoop owns the PTY reader thread and parser, and TD's host.rs TeeReader already copies every read on that thread while holding the lease. libghostty-vt owns no loop, thread or PTY: the embedder calls vt_write. Its Rust handles are !Send + !Sync, so the shadow Terminal must live on one thread. It can be created lazily on alacritty's reader thread (e.g. thread-local per pane) and fed inside TeeReader::read before alacritty parses the chunk. The alternative is a dedicated thread fed through a channel, which loses the ordering that both the attach fence and the a=q reply depend on.
threading_and_loop.note: quote: "Handle types (`Terminal`, `RenderState`, `KeyEncoder`, etc.) are `!Send + !Sync` by design. Callers should drive all operations from a single thread." — [measured] the crate README. TD's host.rs (terminal-delight@426f072:app/src/host.rs:131-132) says "The copy happens *inside* the read, on the reader thread, while the lease is held — which is what makes the attach fence work." Where the shadow should live is my inference.

reply_channel.value: There are two reply channels, and TD must merge them by hand. alacritty emits Event::PtyWrite(String), which TD bounces to the PTY. libghostty-vt calls its write_pty callback (Rust: Terminal::on_pty_write) for every reply it generates, DA and DSR included. To keep 'exactly once', TD must drop every libghostty reply except Kitty APC responses (ESC _ G ...). Ordering matters as well. kitty's detection recipe is a=q followed by DA1, and a terminal that answers DA1 first is judged to lack pictures. So the shadow must parse each chunk, and write its a=q answer, before alacritty answers a DA1 in the same chunk; viu and kitten icat both send a=q and then CSI c in the captures.
reply_channel.note: quote: "To check if a terminal emulator supports the graphics protocol the best way is to send the above *query action* followed by a request for the `primary device attributes <https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DA1.html>`_. If you get back an answer for the device attributes without getting back an answer for the *query action* the terminal emulator does not support the graphics protocol." — [measured] the protocol doc. libghostty-vt 0.2.1 src/terminal.rs L1534-1536: "Call the given function when the terminal needs to write data back to the pty (e.g. in response to a DECRQM query or device status report)." alacritty_terminal-0.26.0 src/event.rs L39-40: "/// Write some text to the PTY. PtyWrite(String),". Capture: terminal-delight@45567b7:docs/plans/program-pixels/evidence/stand-in/viu-kitty.json events (a=q, reply, then q DA1).

td_migration.value: Text-side change: the smallest of any picture option. Seam work: the largest. The seven files, one by one. pane.rs: its 51 grid reads stay. It gains a picture pass that walks the shadow's placements, copied out as Send-able values (image id, generation, RGBA bytes, viewport row/col, grid size, z), and paints them in gpui above or below the text by z. For U=1 it also scans alacritty's cells for U+10EEEE placeholders. host.rs: TeeReader::read feeds a per-pane libghostty Terminal on the reader thread before alacritty parses (thread-local, because the handle is !Send). It enables the file, temp and shm media, installs a PNG decoder, and filters write_pty down to Kitty APC replies. To stop the divergence it must also rewrite the stream: find each direct placement without C=1, inject the equivalent cursor motion into alacritty's input at that byte offset, and forward the rewritten bytes to clients so the replica still hashes equal. That means TD frames Kitty APC itself anyway, which is the approach Zellij takes in front of the same vte 0.15. gridwire.rs: encode_snapshot and grid_hash cover text only. The attach protocol needs a picture message (image bytes plus placements), because the replica window cannot re-read temp or shm transmissions the host already consumed. ReplicaGuard either gains a picture check or treats pictures as host-authoritative. term.rs: the hostless EventLoop path needs the same tap. socketpty.rs: unchanged. main.rs: wiring and config (storage limit, media policy). pane/bench.rs: add a benchmark for the second parser. biggest_risk.value: A direct placement without C=1 is the default in chafa, viu, kitten icat and timg; only mpv sends C=1. On such a placement libghostty moves its cursor right by the image's columns and down by its rows (rows−1 since ghostty's 2026-08-18 fix, the full row count at the crates.io 0.2.1 pin), scrolling when it reaches the bottom. alacritty never sees the APC and leaves its cursor where it was. From the very next byte of text the two grids disagree, and every picture after that is painted at a libghostty row that no longer matches alacritty's cells.
biggest_risk.note: [inferred] Evidence. Kitty protocol doc, L542-549: "After placing an image on the screen the cursor must be moved to the right by the number of cols in the image placement rectangle and down by the number of rows in the image placement rectangle." and "The client can ask the terminal emulator to not move the cursor at all by specifying ``C=1`` in the command". kitty graphics.c L1151-1153: "if (g->cursor_movement != 1 && !g->unicode_placement) { c->x += ref->effective_num_cols; if (ref->effective_num_rows) c->y += ref->effective_num_rows - 1;". screen.c L1610 scrolls: "if (self->cursor->y > self->margin_bottom) screen_scroll(self, self->cursor->y - self->margin_bottom);". libghostty at the 0.2.1 pin (graphics_exec.zig L263-280): "for (0..size.rows) |_| terminal.index()". On main (L382-431) it uses rows−1, after commit afb61e1 "place cursor after tall images properly", which says: "This fixes an incompatibility between Ghostty and Kitty 0.47.1+." Programs. chafa sends "a=T,f=32,s=640,v=418,c=64,r=19,m=1,q=2" (capture chafa-kitty.json:80; source chafa-term-db.c L426). viu sends "f=32,s=640,v=400,c=60,r=18,a=T,t=t" (viu-kitty.json:60; viuer 0.11.0 printer/kitty.rs L284) and then prints \n. kitten icat sends "a=T,q=2,f=100,t=f,s=640,v=400" (icat2-kitty.json:71) and sets C=1 only with --place (kittens/icat/transmit.go L70-72). timg sends "Ga=T,i=%u,q=2,f=100,m=%d" and then "*pos++ = '\n';  // Need one final cursor movement." insights: Divergence table, direct placement (a=T/a=p) without C=1. kitty: x += cols, y += rows-1, then scroll if past the bottom margin. libghostty main: the same, since afb61e1 (2026-08-18). libghostty at crates.io 0.2.1: index() rows times, then x = pin.x + cols. alacritty (vte 0.15): no movement, because the APC is swallowed. The divergence also changes what a person sees, not only where pictures go. After `viu -w 60 pic.png` (r=18) viu prints a newline. In libghostty the prompt lands below the picture; in alacritty it lands on the row under the picture's top row. TD paints the picture from libghostty's pin over alacritty's text, so the picture covers the user's new prompt.

Because vte 0.15 drops APC, a byte-level KittyApcInterceptor runs ahead of vte in TerminalPane::handle_pty_bytes and captures ESC _ G … ESC \ (1 MiB cap per escape). kitty_graphics/parser.rs: actions a=t, a=T, a=p, a=d, a=q; media t=d, t=f, t=t (temp files under /tmp, /dev/shm or named tty-graphics-protocol are deleted); t=s answered ENOTSUPPORTED; formats f=24, f=32, f=100 (PNG decoded to RGBA); o=z zlib; m=0/1 chunking; x/y/w/h source rect, c/r scaling, X/Y cell offsets, z index, C=1; U=1 virtual placements and a=f/a/c animation answered ENOTSUPPORTED. grid_state.rs delete handles d=a/A, i/I, n/N, c/C, p/P, q/Q, x/X, y/Y, z/Z, r/R. replies.rs writes OK or error replies honouring q=; a=q answers OK only when the client's host terminal supports graphics. store.rs keeps a 320 MiB LRU store. (4) pane.rs paints from placements. main.rs and pane/bench.rs change only in wiring. Zellij's host/client model differs from TD's: its client holds no emulator (the server composites and sends a VT line diff per client), so it confirms the host owning truth and writing replies once, but offers nothing for TD's replica-and-hash design.

what_it_is.value: zmx is a small command-line session persister for the terminal, written and maintained by Eric Bower (GitHub neurosnap; sponsored by pico.sh): each session gets its own daemon that owns the PTY, clients attach and detach over a unix socket, and the daemon keeps a libghostty-vt Terminal fed with the same PTY bytes so it can replay the screen and scrollback as VT bytes to a client that re-attaches. It deliberately has no windows, tabs or splits.

kitty_graphics.value: None restored, passthrough live. While a client is attached, every PTY read is broadcast raw to it, so Kitty APC reaches the client's own terminal and draws there if that terminal supports it (pixel sizes are forwarded in the winsize since 0.7.0). grid_api.value: zmx never iterates cells itself. It uses libghostty-vt's Zig API: ghostty_vt.Terminal.init(io, gpa, {cols, rows, max_scrollback_lines, max_scrollback_bytes}); term.vtStream() and vt_stream.nextSlice(bytes) to feed PTY output; term.resize(gpa, {cols, rows}); term.modes.get/set; term.screens.active.pages with getTopLeft(.screen/.active) and pin(.{.active = .{x, y}}) to bound scrollback and viewport; ghostty_vt.Selection.init(tl, br, false); ghostty_vt.formatter.TerminalFormatter.init(term, .vt) with .content and .extra; term.getTitle(), term.getPwd(), term.colors (dynamic fg/bg/cursor); term.screens.active.cursor for logging; ghostty_vt.Parser for input classification.

damage_tracking.value: no — zmx neither reads nor reports damage: each PTY read is forwarded raw to every client and the whole screen is re-serialized only when a client re-attaches.

state_snapshot.value: yes — util.serializeTerminalState(alloc, term) re-encodes the server's libghostty-vt Terminal as VT bytes with ghostty's TerminalFormatter(.vt) and sends them as one Output message, on re-attach only (not first attach): phase 1 = scrollback as styled text with no extras, then CSI 2J / CSI H / SGR 0; phase 2 = the active screen with modes, scroll region, Kitty keyboard and modifyOtherKeys, cursor, charsets and protection; then OSC 7 cwd, OSC 2 title and OSC 10/11/12 dynamic colours. Not carried: palette, tabstops (deliberately), DECSET 2026 (deliberately stripped), per-cell OSC 8 links, the primary screen under an alt screen, and every picture. Against TD's gridwire::encode_snapshot: same strategy (re-emit the grid as VT bytes for a stock emulator), but zmx also carries scroll region, charsets, title, cwd and dynamic colours, which TD does not; both lose the primary grid beneath an alt screen; ghostty's formatter emits modes BEFORE content, where TD restores modes last on purpose; and zmx has no replica emulator on the client and no equivalent of TD's grid_hash check. libghostty-vt also has a binary snapshot API (ghostty_snapshot_*) that zmx does not use.

threading_and_loop.value: zmx owns the whole loop: one double-forked daemon process per session, holding the PTY it created with forkpty(); a single-threaded poll(2) loop over the server socket, the PTY master, a signal pipe and each client socket; every PTY read (up to 4096 bytes) is fed to the libghostty-vt stream and broadcast to clients in the same iteration, so there are no threads, no locks and no snapshot/stream seam to fence. Clients are also single-threaded poll(2) loops that pipe stdin to the socket and Output to stdout.
threading_and_loop.note:
quote: "- The `daemon` and client processes communicate via a unix socket
- Both `daemon` and `client` loops leverage `poll(2)`
- Each session creates its own unix socket file
- We restore terminal state and output using `libghostty-vt`" — [measured] Daemon-per-session: loop.zig L565-572; daemonLoop poll: loop.zig L226-292; PTY: daemonize.zig L84 'spawnPty runs forkpty()'; client loop: loop.zig L16-18. Seam absence inferred from the single-threaded structure.

reply_channel.value: Two regimes. With no terminal client attached, zmx itself scans PTY output for DA1/DA2 queries and queues fixed answers (ESC[?62;22c, ESC[>1;10;0c) into the PTY write buffer; nothing else is answered, because the server's libghostty-vt stream is readonly and ignores queries (Kitty a=q, DSR, XTVERSION go unanswered). With clients attached, queries reach every client's own terminal raw, and only the leader client's input — which carries its terminal's replies — is forwarded to the PTY; a non-leader's input is dropped unless it looks like typing (which makes it leader), so each reply is written once.

td_migration.value: Nothing to adopt as code (zmx is an application); five design points TD's host/replica could borrow, mostly in host.rs and gridwire.rs: (1) resize the host grid to the attaching window's size BEFORE snapshotting, then resize the PTY and SIGWINCH the foreground process group even when the size is unchanged, so TUIs repaint after the snapshot (loop.zig L967-1016); (2) strip DECSET 2026 from the snapshot so a replica does not sit deferring renders; (3) replay title (OSC 2), cwd (OSC 7), dynamic colours and the scroll region, which gridwire.rs does not carry today; (4) answer DA only while no window is attached and otherwise let exactly one leader's replies through — TD already writes replies once from the host, so this is a check, not a change; (5) feed and broadcast on one thread so the snapshot/stream seam cannot exist — TD instead fences alacritty's reader thread with a lease in host.rs. Points NOT to copy: zmx's snapshot has the same alt-screen gap as gridwire, emits modes before content (TD's modes-last order is deliberately safer), drops OSC 8 links and all pictures, and has no equivalent of grid_hash / ReplicaGuard. If TD ever moves its host to libghostty-vt, zmx shows that the formatter can replace gridwire::encode_snapshot for text, and ghostty's binary snapshot (ghostty_snapshot_*) is the better candidate for a libghostty-vt replica; pane.rs, term.rs, socketpty.rs, main.rs and pane/bench.rs are untouched by anything zmx teaches.

bubbles.note: Ghostty itself got the C=0 cursor rule wrong until 2026-08-18. The commit message for afb61e1 reads: "This fixes an incompatibility between Ghostty and Kitty 0.47.1+ ... Kitty defines `C=0` as leaving the cursor after the image and implements the movement as rows minus one, plus one row when the image reaches the right edge" and "(Had to view Kitty source to verify what the spec meant)". The crates.io libghostty-vt 0.2.1 still carries the old rule, moving the cursor a full `rows` down. Any TD code that reproduces the cursor motion must match kitty's source, not the prose spec.
bubbles.why: Any option in which TD tracks Kitty cursor motion itself (alacritty-own-loop, alacritty-patched-vte, ghostty-shadow) inherits this subtlety.

bubbles.note: Host/replica hazard for every picture option. With t=t (temporary file), used by viu, the kitty doc says "the terminal emulator will delete the file after reading the pixel data". With t=s (shared memory), used by mpv --vo-kitty-use-shm, it says the terminal "must read the data from the memory object and then unlink and close it on POSIX". In TD's design the host and the window each parse the same bytes, so only the first reader gets the pixels. Pixels must therefore travel host-to-window over TD's own wire rather than be re-parsed from the byte stream.
bubbles.why: This affects gridwire/attach design for alacritty-own-loop, alacritty-patched-vte, libghostty-vt and ghostty-shadow alike.

bubbles.note: Embedded libghostty-vt ships with Kitty pictures mostly off. The storage limit defaults to 10 MB for the library build (320 MB for the Ghostty app), loading limits default to `.direct` (no file/temp/shm), and PNG works only after the embedder installs a decode callback: "if no `sys.decode_png` hook is specified, png formats are disabled no matter what." So kitten icat (t=f, PNG) and viu (t=t) fail against a default libghostty until the embedder enables those media.
bubbles.why: The libghostty-vt subject's kitty_graphics should say 'implemented but off by default' for file/temp/shm/PNG.

bubbles.note: At the ghostty commit that crates.io libghostty-vt 0.2.1 pins (a887df4, 2026-07-11), the Kitty animation actions answer "ERROR: unimplemented action". Animation (d8b920e, 2026-08-21) and relative placements (cd5f9ee/33ca9e5, 2026-08-20) landed upstream later, and libghostty-rs master (pin 22d1317, 2026-08-06) also predates them. Kitty coverage therefore depends on which ghostty commit the bindings pin, not on ghostty main.
bubbles.why: It keeps the libghostty-vt subject's kitty_tags honest about animation.

bubbles.note: Zellij already solved TD's first problem with the exact parser TD uses: vte 0.15 drops APC (lib.rs L182, SosPmApcString → anywhere), so Zellij puts a 166-line byte-level KittyApcInterceptor in front of it (Ground → Esc → EscUnderscore → Capturing on 'G'; forwards every other byte unchanged; 1 MiB cap per escape; CAN/SUB abort). It is MIT and self-contained, so TD could copy it rather than patch vte — relevant to alacritty-own-loop and alacritty-patched-vte, since it requires only that TD sees the bytes before Processor::advance.
bubbles.why: Removes the 'patch vte' step from the cheapest Kitty path, and it is proven in a shipped release (v0.45.0).

bubbles.note: Zellij's per-client picture replay is a worked answer to 'how does a re-attaching client get the pictures': a HostKittyState per client records which images were transmitted (host id per image/scaled variant) and which placements are live; each frame it deletes freed images (a=d,d=I), deletes stale placements (a=d,d=i,i,p), transmits missing images once (a=t,f=32, 4096-byte chunks, zlib when the host supports it) and re-places changed ones with a=p … C=1. On attach the state is cleared so everything is re-sent. TD's gridwire snapshot could carry pictures the same way.
bubbles.why: TD's host/window replica has no picture story yet; this is a tested design for one.

bubbles.note: Zellij's own Kitty implementation also moves the cursor after a direct placement without C=1: advance_cursor_after_kitty_placement sets x += cols (wrapping to column 0 and one more line if that reaches the width) and adds rows-1 lines; C=1 skips it. And when Zellij re-emits to its host it always sends C=1, so the host's cursor never moves on its behalf — the discipline a shadow emulator would need.
bubbles.why: A second independent implementation (besides kitty's graphics.c) confirms the cursor-movement rule that makes an alacritty+libghostty shadow diverge.

bubbles.note: Zellij forwards queries it cannot answer (CSI 14t/16t pixel sizes, OSC 10/11/4 colours, OSC 52 reads) to a client's host terminal and pauses that pane's parsing until the reply, or a 500 ms cache fallback, lands, so the reply reaches the program at the same stream position the query occupied. It also probes the host with ESC_Ga=q (plain and o=z) followed by a Primary DA barrier at startup to learn Kitty and zlib support.
bubbles.why: TD's host has no display, so pixel-size and colour queries face the same 'only the window knows' problem; this is prior art for answering them exactly once from the host.

bubbles.note: performance_evidence has no throughput figure: Zellij publishes no parse benchmark (no criterion or [[bench]] in the workspace). Only per-cell memory (16-byte TerminalCharacter on x86_64) is sourced. Measuring throughput would mean building and running Zellij, which this round forbids.

At ghostty 8af6897 (2026-08-30) libghostty-vt has a binary state-snapshot feature, on by default: "Terminal state serialization: encode a full terminal (screen contents, scrollback, cursor, styles, modes, etc.) to a compact binary format and decode it back into a live terminal. Used for session persistence, window restoration, and moving terminal state between processes." (C API ghostty_snapshot_*). It sends active state, a READY marker, then history, and it round-trips both screens (TERMINAL record: primary plus optional alternate) — which would close TD's alt-screen gap for a libghostty-vt replica. Caveats: format v1 is 'the work-in-progress format that we intended to continue to break until we can promise binary compatibility', and the Kitty image/placement registry is 'intentionally omitted'.
bubbles.why: Directly answers state_snapshot for the libghostty-vt subject and changes the host/replica calculus: a libghostty-vt host could ship its grid to a libghostty-vt replica without re-encoding it as VT bytes.

bubbles.note: libghostty-vt's VT formatter (the thing zmx uses to restore) emits all modes BEFORE the screen content — "for now for simplicity we just emit them all before" (formatter.zig L408-411) — and emits OSC 8 hyperlinks only for HTML (L1459-1461); it also only formats the active screen (L301-302). TD's gridwire restores modes last precisely because insert/origin/wrap change where painted bytes land.
bubbles.why: If TD swapped to libghostty-vt and used its formatter in place of gridwire, these are regressions to test for (origin/insert mode panes, hyperlinks lost on re-attach).

bubbles.note: Embedded libghostty defaults: kitty_image_storage_limit is 10 MB for the lib artifact (320 MB for the Ghostty app), kitty_image_loading_limits default to '.direct' (no file/temp/shm), and PNG is disabled unless the embedder installs a sys.decode_png hook. A readonly vtStream() still parses and stores Kitty images, it just cannot reply.
bubbles.why: An embedder (TD, or the ghostty-shadow hybrid) must set these three knobs explicitly or icat/chafa PNG transfers and t=f/t=s transfers silently fail.

bubbles.note: zmx avoids the snapshot/stream seam TD fences with a lease by doing everything on one thread, but a newly accepted client is appended to the broadcast list before its Init message is processed (loop.zig L306-325 vs handleInit L949+), so live bytes read in between may reach it before its snapshot. Hunch — not reproduced; phase 2 of the snapshot repaints the visible screen, which probably hides it.
bubbles.why: Prior-art check for TD's handover invariant ('every byte falls on exactly one side').

bubbles.note: Kitty pictures through zmx failed early on because the client's pixel size was not forwarded (issue #14's first report: 'Terminal does not support reporting screen sizes in pixels'); 0.7.0 added xpixel/ypixel to the Init/Resize winsize and sends both 4- and 8-byte encodings for old daemons (ipc.zig L135-138). broot's pixelated Kitty images were reported fixed by 0.7.0 (issue #192).
bubbles.why: TD's host must also propagate TIOCSWINSZ pixel sizes to the PTY, or picture programs refuse to run under the host even when the window can draw them.
